title: Wren and the House
premise: Sebastian Crane, an urban explorer who documents everything as a form of prayer, discovers unmapped tunnels beneath the derelict Crane family estate — tunnels that appear on no survey because the house itself refuses to be counted. When their sleep recordings capture a second voice answering questions in Sebastian's own cadence, they learn the house keeps a ledger of its bloodline, and every generation it 'counts' one heir into its walls. The count is nearly complete. With Wren, the last heir who never knew she was one, Sebastian must unravel which family member the house has already claimed and get them out before the final tally at the winter solstice. In the end, Wren chooses love over duty: she burns the ledger — and her inheritance with it — trading the house's power for her brother's life, leaving Sebastian to document a home that finally, mercifully, stays empty.
about_author: Theo Voss is the pen name of a former building surveyor who spent a decade mapping basements, service tunnels, and spaces official records insist do not exist. They write horror about architecture that remembers, and live in a house they have measured twice.

chapters.title: The Survey That Isn't
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. An urban explorer with a compulsive need to document, Sebastian breaks into the condemned Crane estate and finds a tunnel entrance that appears on no map, no survey, no deed. The emotional beat is thrill curdling into unease when their laser measure returns impossible numbers.

chapters.title: Documentation Is a Kind of Prayer
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian maps the first three tunnels, narrating their recordings like liturgy. The walls are scored with tally marks — thousands, centuries old. Beat: reverence, the explorer's faith that recording a thing makes it safe.

chapters.title: Wren Comes Home
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren returns to the estate to sign demolition papers for a family she barely speaks to. She feels watched by the house itself, and finds fresh chalk marks on a door she remembers being sealed in childhood. Beat: dread wrapped in obligation.

chapters.title: The Second Voice
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Reviewing sleep recordings from nights spent near the estate, Sebastian hears a second voice answering questions they don't remember asking — in their own voice, slightly delayed. Beat: horror of self-estrangement; the archive has turned against its keeper.

chapters.title: Questions Answered
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The voice answers questions about the Crane family with intimate accuracy — including details about Wren. Sebastian realizes the recordings are pulling them somewhere. Beat: compulsion; documentation becomes invocation.

chapters.title: The Ledger in the Walls
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren finds the family ledger hidden behind plaster: names, dates, tallies. Every generation, one entry ends mid-sentence. Her grandmother's line stops in 1974. Beat: cold recognition that her family's wealth was payment.

chapters.title: Pulled Under
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Following the voice into the tunnels, Sebastian loses hours and surfaces inside the house's sealed east wing — pulled straight into the middle of it. Wren finds them there, neither knowing how they got in. Beat: disorientation, first meeting, mutual suspicion.

chapters.title: What the House Counts
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Comparing notes, they decode the ledger's logic: the house counts heirs, and the count completes at the solstice. One name remains unfinished — but the ink is still wet. Beat: urgency ignites; alliance forms out of necessity.

chapters.title: Mother Knows the Words
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren confronts her mother, who recites the counting rhyme without realizing she's doing it. Mother's eyes track something moving along the ceiling. Beat: heartbreak — duty has hollowed the woman who should have warned her.

chapters.title: The Brother Who Stopped Talking
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Wren's brother Eli hasn't spoken in weeks; he only writes numbers. His room's tally marks match the walls'. Sebastian documents him and the recordings capture two voices now — Eli's and the other one, agreeing. Beat: dawning horror that the count has already chosen.

chapters.title: Eviction Notice
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren tries to get the family out; her mother refuses — leaving means forfeiting everything the house provides. Father is worse: he wants the count finished, believing it renews the fortune. Beat: love against duty, first open rupture in the family.

chapters.title: Tunnels Beneath the Tunnels
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Deeper mapping reveals older architecture below — a foundation predating the house, built by people who were counted first. Sebastian's documentation now writes itself while they sleep. Beat: the recorder becoming the recorded.

chapters.title: The Price of Leaving
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren attempts to drive Eli away; the road loops back to the gate no matter the direction. At the property line, Eli's nose bleeds and he mouths the count. Beat: despair — the house won't release what it's counting.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Room
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. They unseal the room where the 1974 entry ended and find evidence the last claimed heir almost escaped — a half-finished escape plan, a burned corner of ledger page. Beat: hope with teeth; someone fought this before.

chapters.title: The Voice Gets a Name
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The second voice introduces itself using Sebastian's full name and begins finishing their sentences in real time. Documentation fails; the recorder captures conversations Sebastian hasn't had yet. Beat: identity dissolution, the book's darkest turn.

chapters.title: Solstice Eve
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The family gathers for the traditional reading — a ritual they've always called a Christmas custom. The mother finally breaks and begs Wren to run alone. Wren refuses to leave Eli. Beat: love against duty made explicit and costly.

chapters.title: The Count Begins
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. At midnight the walls begin tallying aloud, one mark per heartbeat. Doors seal. Sebastian realizes the count isn't choosing Eli — it's choosing whoever holds the ledger. And Wren signed the demolition papers. Beat: catastrophic reversal.

chapters.title: Every Door Leads Down
chapters.summary: Alternating POVS. Fleeing through the house, every exit opens into the tunnels. The second voice offers Sebastian a trade: take Eli's place, become documented forever. Beat: temptation — the archivist offered eternal archives.

chapters.title: The Burning Page
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In the ledger chamber, Wren understands the truth: the house runs on inherited consent. She tears out the unfinished page — her page — and sets it alight, renouncing the inheritance aloud. The house screams through every mouth it owns. Beat: climax; love chosen over duty at maximum cost.

chapters.title: What Remains of the House
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. As the ledger burns, the tunnels collapse inward and the second voice unravels mid-sentence. Sebastian drags Eli toward the collapsing gate, documenting nothing, choosing the living over the record. Beat: sacrifice of the narrator's defining faith.

chapters.title: After the Demolition
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Weeks later: the estate is rubble, the mother diminished but present, Eli speaking again in fragments. Wren keeps the ledger's ash in a jar she cannot bring herself to bury. Beat: grief and relief entangled; inheritance refused but not erased.

chapters.title: One Last Recording
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Epilogue. Sebastian plays their final tape: silence, then breath, then a single new tally scratch — faint, distant, patient. Somewhere under the rubble, the count restarts at zero. Beat: quiet, unresolved dread; the house waits for the next heir.
